title.narrative: LG2 Healthier, Resilient Communities in Small States

description.narrative: The project adopts a dual-track collaborative approach: fulfilling all contractual obligations through June 2026 and beyond while simultaneously establishing an effective health partnership coordination model, as aligned to the new 2025-2030 Strategic Plan. This leverages partnerships across governments, accredited organisations, UN bodies, civil society, and regional actors to transition technical implementation to partners while preserving the Secretariat's unique convening and coordination role. The approach is informed by the Secretariat's proven track record from 2021-2025 in positioning Commonwealth priorities at UN and WHO forums, advancing NCD and youth mental health policies, championing cervical cancer elimination and SRH advocacy, and pioneering climate-health synergies in SIDS. This has established trusted partnerships with WHO, regional health bodies, and member state health ministries, providing the institutional knowledge, credibility, and relationships essential for effective partnership coordination. Binding contractual commitments through June 2026 require responsible completion to maintain institutional credibility and avoid reputational damage or legal liability. If the Secretariat successfully completes all contractual obligations, establishes effective partnership coordination mechanisms with WHO, regional bodies and accredited organisations, and demonstrates the unique value of Commonwealth convening at global forums (WHA, UNGA, climate COPs), it will maintain institutional credibility and member state trust, enable partners to effectively continue health work, and create a viable low-cost coordination model, resulting in a clean exit with obligations fulfilled while establishing a sustainable Health Partnership Coordination role beyond the legacy period. This directly contributes to the Strategic Plan's emphasis on partnerships and the Strategic Accelerator on Resource Mobilisation by transforming health from direct implementation to strategic coordination, demonstrating how the Secretariat amplifies impact through partnership orchestration. The Secretariat's comparative advantage is irreplaceable: neutral convening power across the Commonwealth health architecture; ability to bridge political and technical boundaries through ministerial platforms; deep institutional knowledge and trusted partnerships with small and vulnerable states who lack capacity to engage multiple partners; and strategic positioning to align partner efforts with Commonwealth priorities while ensuring small states' voices remain central to global health agendas.
